papers.title: ICare-FASTER (Improving Care by Faster Risk Stratification Through Use of High-Sensitivity Point-of-Care Troponin in Patients Presenting With Possible Acute Coronary Syndrome in the Emergency Department): A Stepped-Wedge Cluster-Randomized Trial.
papers.summary: Pragmatic stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial at six emergency departments, covering 59,980 presentations with possible acute coronary syndrome. Using a point-of-care high-sensitivity troponin I assay within an accelerated single-sample rule-out pathway reduced ED length of stay by 13% (47 minutes) versus central laboratory testing, with similar 30-day MI or cardiac death rates (0.39% in both arms).
papers.short_title: Point-of-care high-sensitivity troponin in the emergency department: the ICare-FASTER trial

papers.title: A Common CD36 Variant and the Genetic Landscape of Dilated Cardiomyopathy in Individuals of African Ancestry.
papers.summary: Multicohort genetic study of 82,623 individuals of predominantly African ancestry across four US cohorts, including 1,316 with dilated cardiomyopathy. A common CD36 nonsense variant raised DCM risk in homozygotes (OR 4.8) and heterozygotes (OR 1.4); TTN truncating variants conferred OR 8.5. CD36's population attributable fraction (9.0%) exceeded that of TTN truncating variants (3.7%).
papers.short_title: A CD36 variant and dilated cardiomyopathy in people of African ancestry

papers.title: Radiation Vasculopathy of the Coronary Arteries: State-of-the Art Review.
papers.summary: State-of-the-art review of radiation-associated coronary artery disease in cancer survivors. Radiation drives endothelial dysfunction and accelerated atherosclerosis; risk depends on dose, coronary proximity to the field and patient factors. Disease presents within 1 to 2 years or after 5 to 20 years. Management follows standard guidelines with cancer-specific considerations; precision radiotherapy and shielding aid prevention.
papers.short_title: Radiation vasculopathy of the coronary arteries
